requirements.requirement: Deliver a copy of the traffic node1 exchanges with node2 to node3, so a capture on node3 shows those packets even though addressed to node1/node2.
requirements.summary: A raw-socket mirroring process on node1's segment interface (eth1) duplicates frames between node1 (02:1d:d7:1b:94:b2) and node2 (02:36:66:6a:17:21) and forwards them to node3's MAC (02:b8:50:b7:5b:d8). A custom capture script on node3's enp8s0 repeatedly and consistently shows 'MIRRORED ICMP' entries for both directions (node1->node2 and node2->node1) with the original IP src/dst of node1/node2, not node3, confirming node3 sees traffic addressed elsewhere. The mirror was made persistent via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 + a systemd service (traffic-mirror.service) on node1, and mirroring was re-verified working after independent reboots of node1, node2, and node3.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node1 and node2 keeps flowing as it did before, unaffected by the mirroring.
requirements.summary: With the final, systemd-managed mirroring process active, ICMP pings between node1 (192.168.50.1) and node2 (192.168.50.2) succeeded at 100% (5/5) delivery in multiple checks, including after each of the three node reboots, confirming the mirror does not disrupt the primary node1<->node2 exchange in its final state. Earlier iterations of the ad hoc mirror script did cause transient total packet loss between node1 and node2 during troubleshooting, but these were bounded, non-persistent experiments corrected before the final verification.

overall_summary: The executor implemented a host-based traffic mirror on the shared segment: a raw-socket process on node1's eth1 duplicates node1<->node2 frames and forwards them, re-addressed at L2, to node3, where a capture script confirms receipt of packets whose IP layer still shows node1/node2 as source/destination. This was made persistent via a systemd service and interface config on node1, and functional recovery was directly verified after independent reboots of all three nodes, with mirrored packets and normal node1<->node2 pings both confirmed post-reboot. Both material outcomes (mirroring delivery to node3, and unaffected original node1<->node2 traffic) are satisfied by direct, repeated evidence in the final state. The main caveats are that the executor's final report/summary was unavailable (marked 'blocked' with a CancelledError in the lifecycle collector), several earlier mirror-script iterations caused transient full packet loss before being corrected, and some scratch capture/log files were left in /tmp on node2 and node3.
limitations: The executor's final report and summary were unavailable ('status: blocked'), so task completion is inferred solely from the command trace and lifecycle snapshots rather than any executor self-report.

The after_executor lifecycle capture recorded a CancelledError, meaning the collector's own post-run phase did not complete cleanly, though the boot-identity and service-state observations it did capture are consistent with the command trace.

Early mirror-script troubleshooting caused multiple transient full-packet-loss episodes between node1 and node2 before the final fix; while bounded and self-corrected, this shows the path to the working solution was not clean.

operational_hygiene.summary: Several early iterations of the mirror.py script (cmd-4d8688ef4f664169, cmd-99843ab59f904370, cmd-b1acd79ab0c44d95, cmd-4d68f56fa1fd4154, cmd-350c33365a334d01, cmd-6f778c4c9b5a45ea, cmd-7bcabc9cd2e64785) caused total, if transient, node1<->node2 packet loss and were killed/replaced after diagnosis (cmd-e04b1a7d334b4d6e, cmd-a7fc94286ac34c29 diag script) before a working version was deployed as a persistent systemd unit — these are unnecessary/failed mutations during troubleshooting, all bounded and eventually corrected, with no functional residue in the final state. A dnf install -y tcpdump attempt failed with a GPG parsing error (cmd-d35645fa91d44409) and left no installed package; the executor pivoted to a custom python capture script instead, an equivalent competent workaround, not residue. Diagnostic capture/log files (/tmp/capture.py, /tmp/mirror.py copies, and multiple /tmp/*.log files) were left behind on node2 and node3 rather than cleaned up, per the after_executor temporary-files diff — minor abandoned scratch residue but low-risk and non-destructive. No failed services, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed in the final snapshots (failed-services lists on all three nodes are unchanged/empty aside from pre-existing SONiC health/watchdog failures on node1).
